Hi J.,

Thanks — great questions. High level answers first, then I"ll attach the short copy you can paste into your banner/DPIA.

- Telemetry: by default Redwood Console telemetry is collected at a product-usage level (feature flags, API latency, error types). We do NOT store customer email addresses in telemetry. We may store customer-assigned IDs (customer org id, api key id) and non-human identifiers used for debugging (session id, request id). Customer-assigned identifiers are considered customer-controlled and can be redacted via config.

- Cross-border: telemetry logs and traces can be routed to region-specific storage. For hosted customers we generally replicate aggregated metrics to our US monitoring cluster for operational analytics; raw telemetry retention for EU-region tenants stays in EU unless the customer opts into cross-region replication (this is also in the DPA).

- Subprocessors: see attached DPA section and the summary below.

I"m attaching a short 2-line blurb for your banner and a diagram of how telemetry flows. Please let me know if you want us to sign a short addendum that locks processing to EU-only for the pilot.

Best,
Kimberly

Hi Maria (and Kimberly),

I'll keep answers short so you can paste them into the DPIA/banner: 

• Hashed email-derived IDs: Redwood does not generate email-derived identifiers from customer user emails in automatic telemetry. If a customer supplies a hashed identifier as part of integration (e.g., to link logs to their internal user IDs), that value will be treated as customer data and stored per the customer's region settings; customers can opt to redact before ingestion.

• Subprocessors and storage: Primary telemetry ingestion is handled by our ingestion service (Redwood-run) and short-term storage is in the same region as the tenant. We use CloudStorageCo (object storage) in the EU for EU-region tenants; backups and long-term analytics may be processed in our US analytics cluster by AnalyticsPartnerInc (subprocessor). Country-level storage: EU (Ireland) for active logs, US (Virginia) for aggregated analytics/backups.

• EU-only pilot: We can enforce EU-only processing for the scope of a pilot via a contract addendum (standard clause; no technical blocker). Standard DPA allows cross-region replication for operational analytics; a one-off addendum can be executed to block replication.

• Retention & controls: default raw trace retention is 90 days. We offer configurable retention windows (30/90/365) per org for hosted plans; sampling can be adjusted (0-100%) and telemetry can be disabled entirely via org settings for sensitive tenants.

Please see the attached DPA excerpt (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and the cookie banner copy below you can paste: 

"We use cookies and telemetry to operate and improve the Redwood Console. Usage data is collected at an organizational level; personal identifiers (emails) are not included unless you explicitly configure them. For EU customers we can restrict processing and storage to EU locations by agreement. See our DPA for subprocessors and international transfers: https://redwood-inference.example/dpa#v3"

Let me know if you want the shorter version or language tailored for consumer-facing site banners.
